statements.lead: Reported by the South Wales Echo, 12 May 1988:

statements.source_title: South Wales Echo, 12 May 1988 (Legal Wiki EV-0092)

statements.quote: Any advice or correspondence that Cadw may have provided should be preserved in the Royal Commission on the Ancient and Historical Monuments of Wales (RCAHMW) National Monuments Record of Wales (NMRW).

statements.quote: I have searched our electronic records relating to Great House Farm and Barn and I can confirm they were assessed and rejected for listing in the 1988 community survey of Llandough.

statements.quote: The "YYY" marking on the rear of the photo indicates that the buildings were considered marginally below the bar for listing.

statements.lead: The excavators’ report (Holbrook & Thomas, Medieval Archaeology 49, 2005):
statements.quote: At an early stage it became clear that the site contained numerous burials that continued beyond the bounds of the agreed excavation area.
statements.source_title: Holbrook & Thomas 2005 (Legal Wiki EV-0900)

statements.quote: In all 1,026 inhumation burials were examined, by far the largest Early-medieval burial population so far recovered from Wales.
statements.source_title: Medieval Archaeology 49 (2005), abstract (Legal Wiki EV-0293)

statements.quote: This appeal, by the defendant in the action against a decision of Hollis J given on July 24 1986 when he was sitting as a judge of the Queen's Bench Division in Cardiff, raises a novel question of some potential importance under the provisions of the Limitation Acts 1939 and 1980 in relation to the acquisition of title to land by adverse possession.
statements.source_title: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (BAILII)

statements.quote: No such documents were, however, ever produced.
statements.source_title: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (BAILII)

statements.quote: I can see no escape therefore from the conclusion that, whether she liked it or not, from the time of her receipt of the letters, Mrs Buckler was in possession of the farmhouse and garden by the licence of BP Properties Ltd, and her possession was no longer adverse within the meaning of section 10 of the 1939 Act. Accordingly I would dismiss this appeal.
statements.source_title: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (BAILII)

statements.quote: Application declared inadmissible: the fair-trial complaint was not substantiated; the loss of the home was lawful and justified to protect the owner’s rights; there was no “possession” in law because the courts held the property belonged to another.
